OMAHA, Neb. & ATLANTA--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) and Norfolk Southern (NYSE: NSC) today filed their response to Canadian Pacific Kansas City’s request that the Surface Transportation Board (STB) terminate review of the proposed transcontinental railroad, which will be the nation’s first single-line, seamless coast-to-coast railroad.

As made clear in their response and an accompanying verified statement from CEO Jim Vena, Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern consistently support a full, transparent and rigorous review of the proposed merger and encourage all stakeholders to make their views known to the STB.

“I have spoken publicly in front of numerous groups before and since the merger announcement. I have also spoken to and with hundreds of our customers. I do use humor in my presentations to keep the audience engaged, including in my presentation at the conference of the Southwest Association of Rail Shippers this past March. I know what I said and regret the inference. The speech was over 50 minutes long, and I made an attempt at humor at the end of that presentation. I apologize to anyone who misunderstood my statement,” said Vena.

Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern remain focused on advancing a transaction that will give U.S. businesses more options to compete in the global marketplace, lower transportation costs and protect tens-of-thousands of union jobs. The companies look forward to the STB's continued evaluation of the proposed combination based on the facts, evidence and public interest benefits presented in the record. The acquired assets add the Caymus Processing Complex, which includes three processing trains with a total capacity of approximately 675 MMcf/d and approximately 300 miles of pipeline serving leading operators across some of the most active areas of the Delaware Basin.

The transaction is expected to further strengthen Energy Transfer's Permian footprint by increasing access to growing natural gas and NGL production volumes while enhancing connectivity to the Partnership's broader midstream platform.

Energy Transfer LP (TXSE: ET) owns and operates one of the largest and most diversified portfolios of energy assets in the United States, with approximately 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. Energy Transfer’s strategic network spans 44 states with assets in all of the major U.S. production basins. Energy Transfer is a publicly traded limited partnership with core operations that include complementary natural gas midstream, intrastate and interstate transportation and storage assets; crude oil, natural gas liquids (“NGL”) and refined product transportation and terminalling assets; and NGL fractionation. Energy Transfer also owns the general partner interests, the incentive distribution rights and approximately 28 million common units (representing 15% of the aggregate outstanding common units and Class D units) of Sunoco LP (TXSE: SUN), the managing member interests in SunocoCorp LLC (TXSE: SUNC), and the general partner interests and approximately 46 million common units (representing 32% of the outstanding common units) of USA Compression Partners, LP (TXSE: USAC). For more information, visit the Energy Transfer LP website at www.energytransfer.com.

Sunoco LP (TXSE: SUN) is a leading energy infrastructure and fuel distribution master limited partnership operating across 33 countries and territories in North America, the Greater Caribbean, and Europe. This critical infrastructure complements SUN's fuel distribution operations which distribute over 17 billion gallons annually to approximately 11,000 Sunoco and partner-branded retail locations, as well as independent dealers and commercial customers. SUN's general partner is owned by Energy Transfer LP. For more information, visit the Sunoco LP website at www.sunocolp.com.

SunocoCorp LLC (TXSE: SUNC) is a publicly traded limited liability company that owns a direct limited partner interest in Sunoco LP. For more information, visit the Sunoco LP website at www.sunocolp.com.

USA Compression Partners, LP (TXSE: USAC) is one of the nation’s largest independent providers of natural gas compression services in terms of total compression fleet horsepower. USAC partners with a broad customer base composed of producers, processors, gatherers, and transporters of natural gas and crude oil. USAC focuses on providing midstream natural gas compression services to infrastructure applications primarily in high-volume gathering systems, processing facilities, and transportation applications. Regional reliability and grid flexibility work also recognized with additional awards

CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--ComEd customers are served by the most reliable electric utility in the nation. PA Consulting yesterday presented ComEd with its 2026 ReliabilityOne® National Reliability Award, Outstanding Reliability Performance in the Midwest Region and the Grid Flexibility Awards. ComEd previously won the award in 2023.

"Being named the most reliable electric utility in the country is a credit to the dedication of our ComEd workforce and a demonstration of the value of the targeted investments we have made in our grid over the past decade,” said ComEd President and CEO Gil Quiniones. “Our proposed grid plan charts a path for continuing to deliver nation-leading reliability, while keeping affordability top of mind, even in a future with more extreme weather events and unprecedented growth in power demand. We believe that reliability should not come at the expense of affordability, and we are working hard to keep customer bills as low as possible."

The recognition comes as northern Illinois faces new pressures on its power grid. Families and businesses are using more electricity than ever as homes, vehicles and buildings go electric, and severe storms are becoming more frequent and intense. That’s why ComEd’s Grid Plan which will be decided upon in December, is designed to protect the reliability customers count on today and prepare the grid for the decades ahead.

“Congratulations to ComEd on this national recognition, reinforcing Illinois’ nation-leading position in electric reliability,” said Governor JB Pritzker. “As energy demands continue to grow, we remain focused on strengthening our electric grid, lowering costs for working families and businesses, and building a cleaner, more reliable energy future for all Illinoisans.”

Since ComEd began its smart grid investments in 2012, those upgrades have helped customers avoid nearly 27 million power interruptions and more than $5 billion in outage-related costs. Overall reliability, measured by how long customers are without power, has improved by more than 75 percent compared with the 2007–2011 average. Outages lasting 12 hours or more have fallen 69 percent over the same period. These investments include smart switches that automatically reroute power, stronger poles and wires, modernized substations and better storm preparedness. Together, they have also sped up recovery after severe weather. In 2025, ComEd restored power to half of customers affected by storms within two hours and 98 percent within 24 hours. Had it not been for grid investments, an additional 2.6 million customers would have lost power.

“Reliable energy infrastructure is essential to Illinois’ ability to attract investment, support businesses, and create jobs,” said Illinois Economic Development Corporation President and CEO Christy George. “ComEd is an important partner in that work, and this national recognition underscores the strength of our state’s energy infrastructure."

A recent study by ComEd and Argonne National Laboratories projects that the number of heavy rainfall events, as well as more instances of severe weather, in northern Illinois, defined as those producing more than two inches of precipitation, could nearly double by mid-century. To prepare, ComEd is already bringing more durable technologies to the grid like fibreglass poles and elevated substations, developing management strategies to address severe storms, warmer temperatures, invasive pests and tree health risks that can affect vegetation near power lines and planning for new environmental threats that could affect utility equipment and infrastructure.

Severe weather data helps inform grid investments, including ComEd’s latest multiyear grid plan, filed in January, that builds upon its previous plan to strengthen the grid, continue delivering safe and affordable electric service as well as nation-leading reliability for ComEd’s customers amid the challenges of increasingly extreme weather and rising energy demands. The plan aligns with the state’s clean energy and economic development growth goals reflected in the Illinois Climate and Equitable Jobs Act (CEJA) and the Clean and Reliable Grid Affordability Act (CRGA).

Grid Flexibility Award

ComEd also received the ReliabilityOne® Grid Flexibility Award which is presented to a ReliabilityOne® recipient that demonstrated a dedicated focus on providing its customers and grid users with means to cost effectively use the grid to meet their needs. ComEd demonstrated the ability to interconnect a variety of distribution energy resources as well as the ability to monitor and control their outputs to maintain safe, reliable and resilient power throughout the year. These flexible interconnections have been used to defer system upgrades, helping customers get additional value from existing infrastructure investments and enabling clean energy to be added to the system as cost effectively as possible.

ComEd expects to connect approximately 400 community solar projects by the end of 2026 with a little over 320 interconnected year-to-date. Approximately 500 community solar sites are currently within ComEd’s construction interconnection queue, and more than 500 additional projects are currently in the study phase of interconnection to assess system impact. As of October, approximately 8 gigawatts (GW) of renewable generation are interconnected within the ComEd zone, including 6 GW of utility-scale renewable generation and 2 GW of distributed generation resources. Increasing the supply of solar on the grid is critical to meeting the rising energy demands of Illinois.

All utilities operating electric delivery systems in North America are eligible for consideration for the ReliabilityOne® Award. This year we recognize six leading utilities in their respective regions, which include utilities from the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, Upper Midwest, Southeast, and Pacific Regions. The selection of provisional recipients is based primarily on system reliability statistics that measure the frequency (SAIFI) and duration of customer outages (SAIDI and CAIDI). After provisional recipients are selected, each company undergoes a rigorous certification process which provides an independent review and confirmation of the policies, processes and systems used to collect, analyze and report a company's reliability results. Additional awards are recognized based on analysis of certification findings.

About ComEd

ComEd is a unit of Chicago-based Exelon Corporation (NASDAQ: EXC), a Fortune 200 company and one of the nation’s largest utility companies, serving more than 10.7 million electricity and natural gas customers. ComEd powers the lives of more than 4 million customers across northern Illinois, or 70 percent of the state's population. For more information visit ComEd.com, and connect with the company on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, X, and YouTube.

About PA Consulting

PA Consulting believes in the power of ingenuity to build a positive human future. As strategies, technologies and innovation collide, we create opportunity from complexity. Our diverse teams combine deep expertise, innovative thinking and breakthrough technologies to help clients adapt, transform and achieve enduring results across consumer and manufacturing, defense and security, energy and utilities, financial services, government and public services, health and life sciences, and transport. As a Jacobs company, we combine strategic advisory, design and delivery as a single partner across the full program lifecycle. Together, our global team of approximately 47,000 help clients shape investment decisions, solve complex challenges and deliver lasting outcomes. Discover more at paconsulting.com and connect with PA on LinkedIn and X. PA. Bringing Ingenuity to Life.

PA Consulting’s ReliabilityOne® Awards are presented to electric utilities providing their customers with the highest levels of reliability in the industry. PA Consulting’s ReliabilityOne® study is based on standard industry reliability statistics that measure the frequency and duration of electric power outages. As a group, customers of ReliabilityOne® participants on average experienced over 56% fewer sustained outages, and their collective system saw 64% shorter outage durations than the average US investor-owned utility. PA Consulting has been analyzing electric utility performance since 1987. For more information, about PA Consulting, visit https://www.paconsulting.com/industries/energy-and-utilities

Transaction Advances Strategic Rotation into Corporate Payments

Transaction expected to be accretive to 2027 EPS

Company will host an investor call at 6:00pm ET today to discuss the transaction

ATLANTA--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Corpay, Inc. (NYSE: CPAY), the global spend management company, today announced that it has signed a definitive agreement to make a $1.1 billion minority investment in BILL (NYSE: BILL) as part of a transaction to take BILL private alongside TPG for $63.25 per share that values BILL at $6.0 billion.

Under the agreement, Corpay will invest $1.1 billion for an approximately one-third equity stake in the company with the option to acquire 100% of the company. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approval and standard closing conditions.

BILL is an intelligent finance platform and leading provider of spend management and accounts payable solutions to small and lower middle market businesses, with an especially unique distribution network of accountants.

“We’re delighted to partner with BILL leadership and TPG on this transaction. Given our successful relationship with TPG, we are excited to participate in this transaction and invest in another large, complementary corporate payments business,” said Ron Clarke, Chairman and CEO of Corpay.

“We expect the transaction to be accretive to Corpay cash EPS in 2027, and the take-private transaction structure gives the company the flexibility to transform and accelerate profit growth. We have the option to buy the rest of the company in 2030,” said Peter Walker, CFO of Corpay.

“Corpay has a long track record of driving value through innovative products and high-quality customer service,” said John Flynn and Tim Millikin, Partners at TPG. “This joint investment is grounded in a shared conviction in the long-term growth opportunities across financial technology and payments where our respective expertise and capabilities will further support BILL’s next chapter of growth.”

Barclays acted as exclusive financial advisor to Corpay, and Sullivan & Cromwell LLP acted as legal counsel to Corpay.

It matters to investors because it shows how much of the company’s “pie” each share represents—higher EPS usually signals greater profitability per share, helps compare companies of different sizes, and influences stock valuations and investor decisions.

take-private transactionfinancial
A take-private transaction is when one party buys enough shares of a publicly traded company to remove it from the stock market and make it privately owned. For investors this matters because buyers typically offer a cash premium to persuade shareholders to sell, after which shares stop trading publicly and liquidity and public oversight decrease — similar to buying out co-owners of a shared property so it becomes a single-owner house.

First Half 2026 Financial Results

Revenues

Revenues increased by 26.45% to $0.74 million for the first half of 2026 from $0.59 million for the same period of the prior year. The increase was primarily attributable to the renewal of leases with the Company's major tenants and the addition of a small number of new tenants, supported by the Company's continued focus on service quality and the efficiency of its leasing process. The Company believes that maintaining long-term, stable relationships with its tenants supports a stable base of rental income. Subject to market conditions and the other factors described under "Safe Harbor Statement" below, the Company expects revenue from its commercial real estate leasing business to continue to grow in the near term.

Cost of revenues

Cost of revenues consisted primarily of lease and occupancy costs, depreciation and amortization costs, as well as agency-service costs and property maintenance costs. Cost of revenues increased by $0.23 million, or 45.05%, to $0.74 million for the first half of 2026 from $0.51 million for the same period of the prior year. The increase in cost of revenues was primarily attributable to the increase in operating costs related to the leasing business.

Gross profit and gross profit margin

Gross profit was $4,142 for the first half of 2026, compared with $0.08 million for the comparable period in the prior year. The gross profit margin was 0.56% for the six-month period ended June 30, 2026, versus 13.31% for the six-month period ended June 30, 2025, representing a decrease of 12.75 percentage points. The concurrent declines in gross profit and gross profit margin were primarily driven by higher operating costs, which caused cost of revenues to grow at a faster rate than revenues.

Operating expenses

Operating expenses consist of selling expense and general and administrative expense.

Selling expense increased by $31,016, or 1,138.20%, to $33,741 for the first half of 2026 from $2,725 for the same period of the prior year. The increase was mainly attributable to the Company's enhanced marketing and tenant promotion activities, as well as the increased business development efforts to attract new tenants for its commercial real estate leasing business.

General and administrative expense was $0.73 million for the first half of 2026, representing an increase of $0.08 million, or 12.68%, compared with $0.65 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was attributable to higher corporate-level operating expenses to sustain the Company's day-to-day business activities.

As a result, total operating expenses increased by $0.11 million, or 17.40%, to $0.76 million for the first half of 2026 from $0.65 million for the same period of the prior year. The increase was mainly attributable to higher selling expenses as well as higher corporate-level operating expenses to sustain the Company's day-to-day business activities.

Operating loss

Loss from operations was $0.76 million for the first half of 2026, compared to $0.57 million for the same period of the prior year. The increase in operating loss was mainly due to the significant decline in gross profit and the increase in operating expenses, which were not fully offset by the growth in revenue.

Other income, net

Total net other income (expense) decreased by approximately $9.60 million, from net other income of $1.97 million in the six months ended June 30, 2025, to net other expense of $7.62 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026. The decrease was primarily attributable to the net investment loss recognized on the Company's short-term investments. The Company invested its available cash on hand in equity securities of certain publicly listed companies through various open-market transactions. Our investments in marketable securities are accounted for pursuant to ASC 321 and reported at their readily determinable fair value as quoted by market exchanges in the consolidated balance sheets, with changes in fair value recognized in earnings. During the first half of 2026, the fair value of these investments declined, resulting in a net investment loss of $7.62 million, compared with a net investment gain of $2.58 million in the same period of the prior year.

Net income attributable to the Company and earnings per share

As a result of the above, net loss attributable to the Company was $8.34 million, or net loss per share of $0.81, for the first half of 2026, compared to net income attributable to the Company of $1.38 million, or earnings per share of $0.13, for the same period of the prior year. The change was primarily driven by the net investment loss on short-term investments and the decline in gross profit during the period.

Financial Conditions

As of June 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $13.15 million, compared to $19.14 million at December 31, 2025. Accounts receivable were $75,810 as of June 30, 2026, compared to $75,346 at December 31, 2025. We also had short-term investments of approximately $12.00 million and $14.53 million as of June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively, which are highly liquid and can be converted into cash and used in our operations if needed. The decrease in cash and cash equivalents was mainly due to the net cash used in operating and investing activities during the period, including net purchases of short-term investments. The decrease in short-term investments was mainly due to the decline in the fair value of these investments, which resulted in a net investment loss of $7.62 million, partially offset by net purchases during the period.

Net cash used in operating activities was $0.94 million for the first half of 2026, compared to net cash provided by operating activities of $0.29 million for the same period of the prior year. The change was primarily due to the operating loss incurred during the period and changes in operating assets and liabilities.

Net cash used in investing activities was $5.07 million for the first half of 2026, compared to net cash provided by investing activities of $0.07 million for the same period of the prior year. The change was mainly attributable to the increased net purchases of short-term investments during the period, as the proceeds from the sale of short-term investments were lower than the purchases of short-term investments.

There was no cash provided by or used in our financing activities during the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

BILL will be acquired for $63.25 per share in an all-cash transaction, representing a fully diluted equity value of approximately $6.0 billion

SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--BILL (NYSE: BILL), the intelligent finance platform trusted by nearly 500,000 businesses to manage, move, and maximize their money, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by TPG, a leading global alternative asset management firm, in partnership with Corpay (NYSE: CPAY), the Global Spend Management Company. BILL will be acquired for $63.25 per share in a cash transaction that values BILL at $6.0 billion. TPG will acquire a majority interest in BILL through TPG Capital, the firm’s U.S. and European private equity platform, and Corpay will acquire a minority interest.

The per share purchase price represents a 31% premium to the 60-day volume-weighted average price ending on November 16, the last full trading day preceding media reports that BILL was in acquisition discussions.

“This transaction marks an exciting new chapter for BILL, delivering significant, certain, and immediate value to our stockholders, while creating new opportunities to accelerate our transformation and deliver greater value to customers,” said René Lacerte, CEO and Founder of BILL. “With our new partners, we will have the resources, expertise, and strategic support to accelerate innovation, advance our AI transformation, and continue to drive the future of financial operations. We look forward to the opportunities ahead for our customers and our business.”

“BILL has built a differentiated financial operations platform that helps small and midsize businesses manage their most critical financial workflows. We have long recognized the significant opportunity at the intersection of financial technology, AI, and payments, and believe BILL is well positioned to capitalize on these trends through its scaled network, integrated technology, and deep customer relationships,” said John Flynn, Partner at TPG. “We are excited to partner with the BILL team, combining TPG’s technology investing and business-building experience with Corpay’s payments expertise to accelerate innovation and support the company's next chapter,” added Tim Millikin, Partner at TPG.

“We’re excited about the potential this agreement represents and have great respect for everything the BILL team has accomplished. We see clear opportunities to support and complement BILL’s product roadmap, platform capabilities, and the services it offers to a broader range of customers. We look forward to working with BILL to further enhance its market-leading platform to deliver greater innovation and value to customers,” said Ron Clarke, Chairman and CEO of Corpay.

Transaction Details
The transaction, which was approved unanimously by the BILL Board of Directors, is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions, including approval by BILL stockholders and the receipt of required regulatory approvals. There are no financing conditions to the transaction. Starboard Value, BILL's largest stockholder, and BILL’s CEO and Founder, René Lacerte, have agreed to vote their shares in favor of the agreement.

Upon the close of the transaction, Mr. Lacerte will continue to lead BILL as CEO. BILL will become a privately held company, and its common stock will no longer be listed on any public stock exchange.

Advisors
Goldman Sachs and Qatalyst Partners are serving as financial advisors to BILL, Fenwick & West LLP is serving as BILL’s legal advisor, and Joele Frank, Wilkinson Brimmer Katcher is serving as strategic communications advisor.

BofA Securities, Inc., Deutsche Bank Securities Inc., and RBC Capital Markets, LLC are serving as financial advisors to TPG. Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP is serving as legal counsel.

Barclays is serving as financial adviser to Corpay. Sullivan & Cromwell LLP is serving as legal counsel.

About BILL
BILL (NYSE: BILL) is the intelligent finance platform trusted by nearly half a million businesses and their accountants to manage, move, and maximize their money. BILL powers businesses ranging from fast-moving startups to growing companies with complex operations. We use AI to deliver strategic finance capabilities in one integrated platform that includes AP, AR, expenses, forecasting, procurement and more. With a member network of more than 9 million, BILL’s platform processes over 1% of US GDP annually. Headquartered in San Jose, California, BILL is a trusted partner of leading U.S. financial institutions, accounting firms, and software providers. For more information, visit bill.com.

About TPG
TPG is a leading global alternative asset management firm, founded in San Francisco in 1992, with $346 billion of assets under management and investment and operational teams around the world. TPG invests across a broadly diversified set of strategies, including private equity, impact, credit, real estate, and market solutions, and our unique strategy is driven by collaboration, innovation, and inclusion. Our teams combine deep product and sector experience with broad capabilities and expertise to develop differentiated insights and add value for our fund investors, portfolio companies, management teams, and communities.

About Corpay
Corpay (NYSE: CPAY), the Global Spend Management Company, is an S&P 500 company with three primary B2B solution sets. Spend Management, provides corporate and virtual card programs and AP automation solutions. Cross-Border, helps businesses manage foreign-currency exposure and provides global multi-currency account solutions. Vehicle Solutions, controls fuel, tolls, parking and related vehicle spend. With Corpay, the more a business controls, the less it spends. To learn more, visit corpay.com.

Key Terms

fully diluted equity valuefinancial
Total market value of a company's equity after hypothetically converting every currently outstanding, potentially dilutive instrument into common shares — including in-the-money stock options and warrants, restricted stock units, and convertible securities. It is calculated by adding the market value of existing shares to the shares that would be created by exercising or converting those instruments (often applying the treasury-stock method for options/warrants and the if-converted method for convertibles), so the result shows the company's equity value on a “fully converted” share count basis. This number differs from enterprise value and depends on specific conversion assumptions and how exercise proceeds are treated.
all-cash transactionfinancial
An all-cash transaction is a deal where the full purchase price is paid immediately in cash or cash equivalents, rather than through financing or installment payments. For investors, this type of transaction often indicates a quick, straightforward sale and can signal confidence from the buyer, potentially affecting the value and perception of the involved assets.
volume-weighted average pricefinancial
Volume-weighted average price (VWAP) is the average price of a stock over a specific time period where each trade is weighted by the number of shares traded, so larger trades influence the average more than small ones. Investors and traders use VWAP as a reference point to judge whether trades are happening at relatively good or poor prices—like checking the average price paid for an item at a market where bulk purchases count more than single-item buys.
proxy statementregulatory
A proxy statement is a document companies send to shareholders ahead of a meeting that lays out the items up for a vote—like who will sit on the board, executive pay, and major corporate decisions—and provides background so shareholders can decide how to cast their votes or appoint someone to vote for them. Think of it as an agenda plus a ballot and briefing notes, important because the outcomes can change control, strategy, and value.

OLD GREENWICH, Conn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Ellington Credit Company (NYSE: EARN) ("we") today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Highlights

  • Net asset value (NAV) per share was $4.04 as of September 30, 2026, which includes the effects of distributions of $0.24 per share for the quarter.
  • GAAP net income was $3.7 million, or $0.09 per share.
  • Net investment income ("NII") was $6.7 million, or $0.17 per share.
    • Adjusted net investment income1 was $6.7 million, or $0.17 per share.
  • CLO portfolio was $332.0 million as of September 30, 2026.
    • CLO debt investments—$146.4 million
    • CLO equity investments—$185.6 million
    • Purchased $41.5 million of CLO investments and sold $31.5 million, across 61 trades.
  • Weighted average GAAP yield2 for the quarter, based on amortized cost, was 12.9% on the total CLO portfolio.
  • Received $14.5 million in recurring cash distributions3 from the CLO portfolio, or $0.37 per share.
  • Raised net proceeds of $5.5 million through the issuance of approximately 1.27 million common shares at prices representing a 3% weighted average premium to NAV per share.
  • Subsequent to quarter end, reset our monthly distribution rate to $0.05 per share, effective with the distribution payable in January 2027.

Management Commentary

“Ellington Credit generated an economic return of 2.4% for the third calendar quarter, or 9.9% annualized, as our active trading and disciplined risk management helped us navigate renewed market volatility,” said Laurence Penn, Chief Executive Officer and President. “Our CLO mezzanine debt and equity portfolios both contributed positively, led by net investment income. Our credit hedges generated gains for the quarter and helped protect NAV per share as credit spreads widened in September. These positive contributions were partially offset by losses on interest rate hedges associated with our fixed-rate unsecured notes. We are proud to have continued our relative outperformance, generating positive GAAP earnings in a challenging quarter when the vast majority of our peers reported losses.

“We remained highly active during the quarter, executing 61 distinct CLO trades and continuing to rotate capital toward investments where we see more attractive risk-adjusted returns. Our overall portfolio size was roughly unchanged quarter over quarter, as sales, paydowns and deal calls largely offset new investment activity. Importantly, the weighted average yield on assets acquired during the quarter increased to 16.7%, up from 14.9% in the second quarter.

“Adjusted net investment income increased by $0.02 sequentially to $0.17 per share, and we continue to see opportunities for further increases through additional capital deployment, selective use of leverage, and continued portfolio rotation. Our Board of Trustees has reset our monthly distribution rate to $0.05 per share, or $0.15 per quarter, a level supported by our current NII. We believe that this positions us to maintain an attractive, sustainable distribution that is well covered by net investment income, while also building NAV per share.”

CLO Performance

During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Morningstar LSTA U.S. Leveraged Loan Index generated a total return of 1.9%, despite persistent credit dispersion and renewed volatility toward quarter end. Returns were supported by investor demand for floating-rate assets, a recovery in certain discounted loans, particularly in the software sector, and refinancings and maturity extensions. Double-B- and single-B-rated loans generated positive returns over the quarter, while triple-C-rated loans underperformed as rising interest rates pressured highly leveraged borrowers, particularly in cable and telecommunications. Loan prices declined in late September amid heightened inflation concerns and broader market volatility.

The European leveraged loan market underperformed the U.S. market, with more pronounced weakness in lower-quality credits. Headwinds included uncertainty over France’s fiscal and political outlook, energy-price volatility, and some forced selling from European credit funds.

CLO performance was mixed, as constructive loan-market technicals were tempered by the late-quarter selloff. Within CLO mezzanine debt, shorter-spread-duration, more seasoned positions benefited from stronger performance in shorter-maturity loans and principal paydowns that reduced deal-level leverage and strengthened structural credit protections. Meanwhile, higher-quality CLO equity positions with longer reinvestment periods benefited from stronger-than-anticipated interest payments in July, while limited loan repricing activity continued to support excess spread and equity cash flows.

However, higher borrowing costs pressured highly leveraged borrowers, weighing on CLO investments — particularly European CLO equity and lower-rated debt positions — with greater exposure to lower-quality collateral. In September, CLO tranche spreads widened modestly, and CLO equity valuations came under renewed pressure as broader markets weakened.

Our CLO mezzanine debt and equity portfolios each generated positive results for the quarter, as net investment income more than offset net realized and unrealized losses in our CLO equity investments. Credit hedges generated gains for the quarter overall, including in September, helping cushion the impact of that month’s spread widening on NAV per share. Additional headwinds included losses on interest rate hedges associated with our unsecured notes, and mark-to-market losses on the notes themselves as credit spread tightening more than offset the impact of higher interest rates.

We executed 61 distinct CLO trades during the quarter, with sales and paydowns largely offsetting new investment activity. The weighted average yield on assets acquired during the quarter increased to 16.7%, compared with 14.9% in the second quarter. At September 30, 2026, our CLO portfolio had a fair value of $332.0 million and a weighted average projected yield of 18.3% based on fair value.

Key Terms

collateralized loan obligationsfinancial
A collateralized loan obligation is a financial product that pools many corporate loans and repackages them into slices sold to investors, with some slices offering steady, lower returns and others offering higher returns but more risk. Like splitting a pizza into pieces for different tastes, CLOs let investors pick their preferred risk level and help banks fund lending, so changes in CLO performance influence credit availability and can move markets.
net asset valuefinancial
Net asset value is the total value of an investment fund's assets minus any liabilities, divided by the number of shares or units outstanding. It represents the per-share worth of the fund, similar to how the value of a house is determined by its total worth after debts are subtracted. Investors use it to gauge the true value of their holdings and to compare different investment options.
View in glossary
non-GAAP financial measurefinancial
A non-GAAP financial measure is a way companies present their financial results that excludes certain expenses or income to show how they believe their core business is performing. It matters because it can give a clearer picture of how the company is really doing, but it can also be used to make results look better than they actually are.
total return swapsfinancial
A total return swap is a contract where one party agrees to pay another the full economic performance—price changes plus income—of an asset, while the other party pays a regular fee or interest. Think of it like renting the gains and losses of a stock or bond without owning it: investors can gain exposure, hedge positions, or add leverage more cheaply, but they take on the risk that the counterparty might fail to honor payments and that synthetic holdings can affect leverage and transparency.

All amounts are in U.S. dollars unless otherwise stated.

The Study evaluates the development of a mechanized, ramp-access underground mine focused on the Project’s sulphide mineralization and high-grade core. The proposed operation is designed at 4,000 tonnes per day (tpd) of processing capacity and would produce silver-lead and silver-zinc concentrates using conventional crushing, grinding and flotation, with filtered tailings planned for dry-stack facility.

The Study represents an important milestone in advancing Pitarrilla toward a development decision.   • Key Permits Supporting Development: Key permits are in place for water use and discharge, explosives, change of land use, development and underground mining. Additional approvals and amendments remain outstanding, including the Tailings Storage Facility Permit (TSF)

  • Resilience at Lower Silver Prices: Pitarrilla has an estimated break-even silver price below $30 per ounce, compared with the base-case silver price of $50 per ounce, providing a margin against lower silver prices while maintaining leverage to higher silver prices

  • Capital Investment for Long-Term Growth: Planned initial capital(2) of approximately $585 million, including $65 million of contingency, with sustaining capital(2) of approximately $119 million over the life of mine.   • Well Positioned to Fund Construction: Endeavour expects to fund the majority of construction of Pitarrilla through a combination of cash on hand and cash flow from its operating mines, providing flexibility as the Project advances toward a development decision

  • Mechanized Underground Mining: A ramp-access underground mine is designed to support planned production averaging approximately 4,000 tpd, utilizing long-hole stoping and development in ore

  • Conventional Processing: The processing flowsheet includes crushing, grinding and flotation, followed by concentrate thickening and filtration. Filtered tailings are planned for storage in a dry-stack facility

Location and Access

Pitarrilla is located within the Municipalities of El Oro and Inde, on the eastern flank of the Sierra Madre Occidental mountain range in the central part of Durango State, Mexico. The city of Durango, the capital of Durango state, is located 160 kilometres south of the property and the major city of Torreón 160 kilometres to the east.

Pitarrilla is accessible by regional roads. Planned primary access follows approximately 47 kilometres of existing roads, with secondary access via El Palmito. Required upgrades include a permanent bridge over the Nazas River, approximately 11 kilometres from the property.


Property, History, Geology, Mineralization

Pitarrilla is formed by 5 contiguous mineral concessions entitled to Minera Pitarrilla S.A. de C.V. (“Minera Pitarrilla”) and covering a total area of approximately 4,950 hectares. Minera Pitarrilla is a Mexican corporate entity, and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Endeavour. 

The Sierra Madre mountain range preserves remnants of one of Earth’s largest accumulations of intermediate to felsic volcanic rocks, formed in a calc-alkaline magmatic arc during the Eocene to early Miocene, approximately 52–25 million years ago. This volcanism intermittently generated numerous medium- to high-level hydrothermal systems enriched to varying degrees in Ag, Au, Pb and Zn, including epithermal systems in the major Mexican silver districts of the states of Guanajuato, Zacatecas, Durango and Chihuahua. Pitarrilla’s silver-lead-zinc mineralization lies within the Central Mexican Silver Belt, a metallogenic province encompassing these districts. 

Endeavour purchased Pitarrilla from SSR Mining Inc. (SSR) for $70 million in 2022, consisting of $35 million in common shares and a further $35 million in cash or in common shares at the election of SSR and agreed to by the Company, and a grant of a 1.25% NSR royalty.

Mine Plan and Production Profile

Pitarrilla is planned as a mechanized, ramp-access underground mine capable of supplying approximately 4,000 tonnes per day to the processing plant. The current design contemplates a mining mix weighted toward transverse and longitudinal long-hole stoping, supplemented by development in ore. The mine plan is expected to target the sulphide mineralization, including Manto Pitarrilla and associated feeder structures. The readily accessible Manto Pitarrilla deposit configuration supports an efficient mine layout with relatively limited underground development required over the LOM. Approximately 16.7 kilometres of total development is planned, comprising 5.4 kilometres during the initial years and 11.3 kilometres of sustaining development thereafter, providing access to the deposit while supporting operating flexibility and efficient, low-cost mining. The current mine plan includes stockpiling over 600,000 tonnes of ore during the construction phase.  

Processing and Infrastructure

The proposed 4,000 tpd process plant is expected to include crushing, a grinding circuit incorporating a primary ball mill and a semi-autogenous grinding (SAG) mill, flash, rougher, scavenger and cleaner flotation, concentrate thickening and filtration, and a tailings filtration plant. Filtered tailings are planned to be placed in a dry-stack storage facility. Pitarrilla benefits from year-round road access and an established project footprint with power and water access, exploration infrastructure, contractor facilities and regional access to an experienced workforce.

Capital Investment, Operating Costs and Cash Flow

Initial capital(2) to develop Pitarrilla is estimated at $585 million and is expected to be incurred over a 30-month construction period. Cumulative sustaining capital(2) is estimated at $119 million. Sustaining expenditures are expected to be front-end loaded, as the readily accessible Manto Pitarrilla deposit requires relatively limited development later in the mine life, supporting lower ongoing capital requirements and significant operating flexibility.

LOM average direct production costs(2) are estimated at $109.24 per tonne processed, with cash costs(2), net of by-product credits, of $12.66 per payable oz silver and mine-site AISC(2) (including royalties and special mining duties), net of by-product credits, of $15.06 per payable oz silver.

During full years of commercial production, average annual after-tax free cash flow(1) is estimated at approximately $136 million.

  • Resource Conversion and Mine-Life Extension: Convert additional Inferred Mineral Resources to higher-confidence categories through targeted drilling and evaluate opportunities to incorporate suitable material into future mine plans. The current mine plan is based on a 150 g/t cut-off grade. A sustained higher metal price environment could support a lower cut-off grade, potentially extending mine life significantly by incorporating additional mineralized material with grades modestly below those included in the current mine plan
  • Metallurgical Evaluation: The feasibility study mine plan excludes 18.4 million tonnes of mineral resources within the transition zone. This represents a significant opportunity to further evaluate the metallurgical characteristics of this material and potentially incorporate these resources into future mine plans, leveraging existing infrastructure with minimal additional mine development requirements
  • Exploration Upside: Test extensions of the Pitarrilla mineralization, in feeder structures which remains open at depth, and other priority targets across the property that could add higher-grade tonnes or extend the production profile
  • Future Open-Pit Potential: The underground sulphide strategy preserves the broader resource base, maintaining the potential to evaluate future open-pit development of Indicated and Inferred Mineral Resources, providing an additional pathway for long-term growth and value creation

Cash cost (“Cash cost”) per ounce

Cash cost per ounce is a non-IFRS measure.  In the silver mining industry, this metric is a common performance measure that does not have a standardized meaning under IFRS.  Cash costs include direct costs (including smelting, refining, transportation and selling costs), royalties and special mining duty and changes in finished goods inventory net of by-product credits. 

Mine Site - All-in sustaining costs (“MAISC”) and All-in sustaining cost (“AISC”) per ounce

MAISC and AISC per ounce are non- IFRS measures.  These measures are intended to assist readers in evaluating the total cost of producing silver from operations.  While there is no standardized meaning across the industry for AISC measures, the Company’s definition conforms to the definition of AISC as set out by the World Gold Council and used as a standard of the Silver Institute.  The Company defines AISC as the cash operating costs (as defined above), reclamation cost accretion, mine site expensed exploration, corporate general and administration costs and sustaining capital expenditures. For the purpose of this press release, MAISC does not include corporate general and administration costs or mine site expensed exploration.

Free cash flow

In the mining industry, free cash flow is a common performance measure with no standardized meaning.  The Company calculates free cash flow by deducting cash capital spending (capital expenditures, net of expenditures paid through finance leases) from net cash provided by operating activities.

The Company discloses free cash flow as it believes the measure provides valuable assistance to investors and analysts in evaluating the Company’s ability to generate cash flow after capital investments and build the cash resources of the Company.

Initial and sustaining capital

Initial and sustaining capital are non-IFRS measures.  Initial capital is defined as capital required to develop and construct to bring the mine to commercial production and sustaining capital is defined as the capital required to maintain operations at existing levels.  Both measurements are used by management to assess the effectiveness of an investment program.

Earnings before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization (“EBITDA”)

EBITDA represents net earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.  EBITDA is an indicator of the Company’s ability to generate liquidity by producing operating cash flow to fund working capital needs, service debt obligations, and fund capital expenditures.

Gross revenue and Gross Cost of Sales

Gross revenue represents gross sales of metals and is calculated by adjusting net revenue for the removal of treatment, refining and transportation costs.  Gross cost of sales is calculated by adjusting cost of sales for the inclusion of treatment, refining and transportation costs.

  • With additional patients and longer follow-up, the combination of RASONQUE plus gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel demonstrated deep and durable responses in the first-line treatment setting
  • Results support the ongoing Phase 3 RASolute 303 trial in patients with treatment-naïve metastatic pancreatic cancer

REDWOOD CITY, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Revolution Medicines, Inc. (Nasdaq: RVMD), a global, commercial-stage oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers, today announced encouraging updated results from the Phase 1/2 RMC-GI-102 open-label study evaluating RASONQUE (daraxonrasib) in combination with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel (GnP) as a potential first-line treatment for patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC). The data will be presented today during a late-breaking oral session at the EORTC-NCI-AACR (ENA) Symposium on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics in Barcelona, Spain.

As of September 28, 2026, 61 patients in the first-line metastatic PDAC cohort of the Phase 1/2 RMC-GI-102 open-label study had received RASONQUE (200 mg) plus GnP, with median follow-up of 18.3 months. In the updated analysis, the confirmed objective response rate was 60.7% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 47.3–72.9), including complete responses in 8.2% of patients. The disease control rate was 90.2% (95% CI: 79.8–96.3) and median duration of response was 11.1 months (95% CI: 7.6- 18.4). Median progression free survival (PFS) was 12.8 months (95% CI: 10.8–18.4) and the twelve-month overall survival was 76.6% (95% CI: 63.7-85.4). The safety profile was consistent with the known safety profiles previously observed for both RASONQUE and GnP. This update builds on findings previously presented at the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) Annual Meeting in April 2026.

“With longer follow-up and a larger patient population, we are seeing a notable combination of high response rates, including deep complete responses, and durable disease control, with median progression-free survival exceeding one year,” said Wungki Park, M.D., M.S., medical oncologist at the David M. Rubenstein Center for Pancreatic Cancer Research at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, RMC-GI-102 and RASolute 303 investigator, and presenter of the data at ENA. “The emerging survival signal is meaningful and is estimated at 76.6% for patients to be alive at one year. Taken together, these findings provide a compelling rationale to further evaluate daraxonrasib as a potential first-line treatment option.”

“People with treatment-naïve metastatic pancreatic cancer urgently need more effective treatment options, given the limited clinical benefit of current chemotherapy regimens,” said Alan Sandler, M.D., chief development officer of Revolution Medicines. “The FDA’s recent Breakthrough Therapy Designation for RASONQUE plus GnP in this setting underscores the urgency of this work. The durability of treatment shown with these updated Phase 1/2 results is particularly encouraging and supports the ongoing Phase 3 RASolute 303 trial, which is evaluating RASONQUE both as a monotherapy and in combination with GnP versus GnP alone in patients with treatment-naïve metastatic PDAC, independent of tumor RAS genotype.”

The presentation (8LBA), titled “Daraxonrasib plus Gemcitabine/Nab-Paclitaxel (GnP) as First-Line (1L) Treatment for Patients (Pts) with Metastatic Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma (mPDAC),” will be delivered by Dr. Park during a late-breaking oral session on November 20, 2026, at the ENA Symposium in Barcelona, Spain.

About Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma (PDAC)
Pancreatic adenocarcinoma, or PDAC, is the most common form of pancreatic cancer and among the most challenging malignancies. RAS, a key growth control switch in human cells, is the main driver of pancreatic cancer, which is characterized by excessive RAS signaling. Each year, approximately 500,000 people globally are diagnosed with PDAC and it is the seventh leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide.1,2

Because early-stage pancreatic cancer often causes few or no symptoms, approximately 80% of patients are diagnosed after the disease has spread, when treatment options are more limited.3 For patients with metastatic PDAC, the five-year relative survival rate is approximately 3% worldwide.4

About RASONQUE® (daraxonrasib)
RASONQUE (daraxonrasib) is an oral, RAS(ON) multi-selective, noncovalent, tri-complex inhibitor (TCI), approved by the U.S. FDA for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or who are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy.5 In the European Union, RASONQUE is approved by the European Commission for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy. RASONQUE is being investigated through a global Phase 3 registrational program in patients with PDAC and metastatic RAS mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Outside the U.S. and the European Union, RASONQUE is an investigational agent that has not been approved by any regulatory authority.

U.S. FDA APPROVED INDICATION
RASONQUE is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or who are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION FOR U.S. APPROVED INDICATION
RASONQUE is associated with the following Warnings and Precautions: Dermatologic and Soft Tissue Toxicity, Stomatitis and Oral Disorders, Diarrhea, Gastrointestinal Perforation, Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD)/Pneumonitis, and Embryo-Fetal Toxicity.

WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS

Dermatologic and Soft Tissue Toxicity
RASONQUE can cause dermatologic toxicity, which may be severe. Clinical manifestations included, but were not limited to, rash, pruritus, paronychia, dry skin, and skin fissures. In clinical trials of patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, dermatologic toxicity occurred in 86% of patients treated with RASONQUE, of which 10% were Grade 3.

Monitor patients who develop dermatologic or soft tissue toxicities while receiving RASONQUE. Initiate prophylactic measures (e.g., topical corticosteroids, emollient creams, sunscreen, oral antibiotics) prior to the first dose of RASONQUE to reduce the risk of moderate to severe dermatologic reactions. Advise patients to limit sun exposure while taking RASONQUE. Initiate supportive measures (e.g., oral corticosteroids) as clinically indicated, and consider dermatologic consultation. Withhold, reduce the dose, or permanently discontinue RASONQUE based on severity.

Stomatitis and Oral Disorders
RASONQUE can cause stomatitis, including mouth ulcers and oral mucositis. In clinical trials of patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, stomatitis occurred in 57% of patients, of which 9% were Grade 3.

Monitor patients for signs and symptoms of stomatitis while receiving RASONQUE. Initiate a steroid-containing mouthwash for treatment of stomatitis and administer other topical treatments (e.g., chlorhexidine mouthwash, 2% lidocaine viscous) as clinically indicated. Withhold, reduce the dose, or permanently discontinue RASONQUE based on severity.

Diarrhea
RASONQUE can cause diarrhea. In clinical trials of patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, diarrhea occurred in 63% of patients, of which 6% were Grade 3.
If diarrhea occurs, administer antidiarrheal treatment as clinically indicated. Withhold, reduce the dose, or permanently discontinue RASONQUE based on severity.

Gastrointestinal Perforation
RASONQUE can cause gastrointestinal perforation. In clinical trials of patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, gastrointestinal perforation occurred in 0.9% of patients treated with RASONQUE, of which 0.5% were Grade 3, one event was Grade 4, and one event was fatal.

Monitor patients for gastrointestinal perforation. Withhold RASONQUE if gastrointestinal perforation is suspected. Reduce the dose or permanently discontinue RASONQUE if no other potential causes of gastrointestinal perforation are identified.

Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD)/Pneumonitis
RASONQUE can cause interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis. In clinical trials of patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma, ILD/pneumonitis occurred in 2.4% of patients treated with RASONQUE, of which 0.9% were Grade 3, and one event was fatal.

Monitor patients for new or worsening pulmonary symptoms. Withhold RASONQUE if ILD/pneumonitis is suspected. Reduce the dose or permanently discontinue RASONQUE if no other potential causes of ILD/pneumonitis are identified.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity
Based on findings in animals, RASONQUE can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with RASONQUE and for 1 week after the last dose. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with RASONQUE and for 1 week after the last dose.

ADVERSE REACTIONS
Serious adverse reactions occurred in 30% of patients treated with RASONQUE. Serious adverse reactions occurring in ≥ 2% of patients treated with RASONQUE were diarrhea (3.7%), pyrexia (3.3%), sepsis (2.9%), fatigue (2.1%), and hemorrhage (2.1%).

Adverse reactions leading to permanent discontinuation of RASONQUE occurred in 2.9% of patients, including two patients who discontinued due to rash (0.8%).

The most common (≥ 20%) adverse reactions in patients treated with RASONQUE were rash, diarrhea, stomatitis, nausea, fatigue, vomiting, abdominal pain, edema, decreased appetite, and hemorrhage.

DRUG INTERACTIONS

  • Strong CYP3A Inhibitors with P-gp Inhibition: Avoid concomitant use.
  • Strong CYP3A Inhibitors without P-gp Inhibition: Reduce RASONQUE dosage.
  • Moderate CYP3A Inhibitors with or without P-gp Inhibition: Reduce RASONQUE dosage.
  • P-gp Inhibitors: Reduce RASONQUE dosage.
  • Cyclosporine A: Avoid concomitant use.
  • Strong CYP3A Inducers: Avoid concomitant use. Increase RASONQUE dosage if concomitant use cannot be avoided.
  • Moderate CYP3A Inducers: Increase RASONQUE dosage.
  • P-gp Substrates: Take at least 4 hours apart from RASONQUE.

PROPHYLACTIC MEASURES
When initiating RASONQUE and throughout treatment, prophylactic and concomitant medications are recommended to reduce the risk of dermatologic reactions:

  • administer a topical corticosteroid (applied to the face and chest) and emollient creams;
  • advise patients to limit sun exposure and use broad-spectrum sunscreen (SPF 30 or higher); and
  • consider prophylactic oral antibiotics (e.g., doxycycline or minocycline).

Please see U.S. Full Prescribing Information for RASONQUE.

About Revolution Medicines, Inc.

Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-stage oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide. NORTH PLAINS, Ore., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Jewett-Cameron Trading Company Ltd. (the "Company"; Nasdaq: JCTC), a company committed to innovative products that enrich outdoor spaces, today announced operational and financial results for its fiscal year 2026 ended August 31, 2026.

Highlights include:

  • Revenue of $36.7 million, down 11% from $41.3 million, primarily due to the loss of a major cedar supply customer. Metal fencing sales rose 2% and Greenwood sales rose 33%.
  • Gross margin of 11.0% compared to 15.1%, reflecting higher steel tariffs, higher logistics costs, and inventory liquidations, in part below cost. Results include $1.1 million of non-recurring refunds of tariffs that were invalidated by the U.S. Supreme Court.
  • Net loss of $6.4 million, or $(1.81) per share, compared to $4.1 million, or $(1.18) per share. The net loss narrowed each quarter, to $(0.11) per share in the fourth quarter.
  • Operating cash flow of $3.7 million, compared to cash used of $6.6 million in fiscal 2025.
  • Balance sheet: inventory reduced to $6.5 million from $15.9 million, all bank borrowings repaid, and cash of $1.9 million at August 31, 2026. The Northrim credit facility was renewed through June 30, 2027.
  • Cost reduction: full-time headcount reduced to 34 from 45, and wages and benefits down 14%.
  • Seed property sale: after year-end, the Company agreed to sell its former seed property to Washington County for $5.9 million. The sale is subject to the County’s 180-day extendable due diligence period, during which it may terminate the agreement, the approval by the Washington County Board of Commissioners, and certain other conditions.  The sale carries real estate commissions of 5% due at closing.

“We converted excess inventory to cash, repaid our bank debt, and lowered our cost structure in a difficult tariff environment,” said Chad Summers, CEO. “Margins remain under pressure, and we are focused on improving liquidity and protecting the value of the Company.”

The Company remains committed to the implementation of its strategic realignment that prioritizes higher margin products and the Company’s overall value. Management and the Board continue to evaluate strategic alternatives, which may include a sale of the Company or of some or all of its assets or business lines, or other transactions. There can be no assurance that these discussions will result in definitive agreements or the completion of any transaction. The Company does not intend to provide further updates on these discussions unless and until a definitive agreement is reached.

About Jewett-Cameron Trading Company Ltd. (JCTC)
Jewett-Cameron Trading Company Ltd. is a trusted provider of innovative, high-quality products that enrich outdoor spaces.
